target.title: fix(sessions): prune stale entries independently of maxEntries gate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issue #103956: the `session.pruneAfter` configuration setting is silently ignored during normal gateway operation. Sessions older than the configured prune cutoff grow unbounded regardless of the `pruneAfter` duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

During load-time session store maintenance, stale-entry pruning (`pruneStaleEntries`) was gated by `Object.keys(store).length > maintenance.maxEntries`. This meant age-based pruning only fired when the store exceeded its entry count limit. If a user had fewer sessions than `maxEntries` (default 500), no pruning ever happened ??`pruneAfter` effectively became dead configuration.

The fix separates the pruning trigger from the entry-count gate, matching the established pattern in `applyEnforcedMaintenance()` in `store-maintenance-operations.ts` which already runs `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally in enforce mode.

## User Impact

Users who configure `session.maintenance.pruneAfter` will now see sessions older than the configured duration automatically removed during load-time maintenance, regardless of how many sessions exist. The entry-count cap (`maxEntries`) continues to work exactly as before ??it is still gated by `shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance`.

## Evidence

**Root cause**: In `src/config/sessions/store-load.ts`, the `pruneStaleEntries` call at load-time was inside an `if` condition `maintenance.mode === "enforce" && Object.keys(store).length > maintenance.maxEntries`. Removing the entry-count gate restores independent age-based pruning.

The fix is a structural mirror of `applyEnforcedMaintenance()` in `store-maintenance-operations.ts`, which already runs `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally (when mode is `"enforce"`):

```typescript
// store-maintenance-operations.ts (correct behavior ??runs pruning unconditionally)
const pruned = pruneStaleEntries(store, maintenance.pruneAfterMs, { ... });
const countAfterPrune = Object.keys(store).length;
const shouldRunCapMaintenance = shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance({ ... });
```

```typescript
// store-load.ts (after fix ??same pattern)
pruned = pruneStaleEntries(store, maintenance.pruneAfterMs, { ... });
const countAfterPrune = Object.keys(store).length;
capped = shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance({ ... }) ? capEntryCount(...) : 0;
```

Diff: only `src/config/sessions/store-load.ts` ??3 lines changed, 1 removed.

Evidence tier: L2 (vitest + fixture)
Proof limitations: Unit-level verification covers pruning logic and the load-time path.

## Tests

```powershell
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts --no-coverage --reporter=basic
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts --no-coverage --reporter=basic
pnpm check:changed
pnpm format:check
```

## Risk

- Behavior change: Yes ??stale pruning now works as documented
- Config change: No
- Data loss risk: Low ??pruning uses the same `pruneAfterMs` threshold already configured; no new deletion path
- Performance impact: Low ??`pruneStaleEntries` is O(n) on session count and was already called during every load-time maintenance pass when over the entry limit

## Current Review State

Ready for review.

---

target.title: fix(tlon): cap SSE payload JSON.parse at 16 MiB to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`parseUrbitSsePayload()` and `processStream()` in `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.ts` have two unbounded memory paths on external Urbit ship SSE data:

1. **Stream buffer accumulation** (primary): `processStream` appends chunks into `buffer` with no byte cap. A hostile ship can send an unterminated SSE event (no `\n\n`) and exhaust memory before any event is dispatched.
2. **JSON.parse** (defense-in-depth): `parseUrbitSsePayload` calls `JSON.parse(data)` with no size limit, allowing a large single event to OOM.

Both paths are now capped at 16 MiB, matching the merged pattern in `extensions/signal/src/client.ts` (bounded SSE buffer + bounded event data).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Stream buffer**: Added incremental `Buffer.byteLength` tracking in `processStream`. The byte-limit check runs **before** `buffer += chunkStr` so a single oversized chunk never lands in the pending buffer — the guard protects memory, not just the byte counter.
- **Parse guard**: Retained as defense-in-depth — oversized events that slip through the stream cap (e.g., `\n\n`-delimited but individual event data > 16 MiB) are still rejected at parse time.

Pattern aligned with Signal SSE (`extensions/signal/src/client.ts:36-37`, `MAX_SIGNAL_SSE_BUFFER_BYTES` / `MAX_SIGNAL_SSE_EVENT_DATA_BYTES`) and the 16 MiB constants used across `extensions/google/`, `extensions/feishu/`, `extensions/xai/`, etc.

## User Impact

- Normal SSE events processed unchanged
- Stream buffer exceeding 16 MiB: logged + stream error handler invoked + auto-reconnect
- No change to malformed JSON handling or small-event behavior

## Evidence

- **Bug exists on main**: both `processStream` (unbounded `buffer +=`) and `parseUrbitSsePayload` (raw `JSON.parse`) lack size guards
- **No competing PR**: full search across `parseUrbitSsePayload`, `sse-client`, tlon+SSE, unbounded+OOM
- **Tests**: 22/22 passed, including 4 stream-path tests:
  - oversized 17 × 1 MiB chunks without `\n\n` → rejected at buffer cap (multi-chunk overflow)
  - **single oversized chunk (17 MiB) → rejected before concatenation** (guard ordering proof)
  - normal `\n\n`-delimited event → handler receives `{ok: true}`
  - 1000 small events → all delivered, buffer trim path exercised
- **Production-style proof**: `extensions/tlon/proof-sse-bounded.mts` drives real `UrbitSSEClient.processStream` and `processEvent` against Node `Readable` streams, with negative control against `origin/main`

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --run
Tests: 22 passed (22)
```

**Negative control (origin/main):**

```
main: unbounded buffer += chunkStr → OOM
fix:  buffer cap checked BEFORE concatenation → rejected safely
```
